name: CA-16
label: Safe D

key_factors: Prediction markets price a Liccardo win near 97%
Incumbent running with no outside spending against him
model.rationale: The district's 25-point Democratic lean, Liccardo's overwhelming fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 97% all point to a comfortable incumbent win; with no polls or expert ratings available, the structural fundamentals leave little room for doubt.
model.watch: A late scandal or a sudden surge of outside spending for Soulé is the only plausible path to making this race competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 16th District leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan lean of about 25 points, and incumbent Sam Liccardo is seeking re-election after advancing to the general election. His Republican challenger, Peter Soulé, has reported only $400 in total fundraising, while Liccardo has raised roughly $3.5 million and holds more than $2.1 million on hand. No outside groups have invested meaningfully on either side.

Prediction markets put Liccardo's chances near 97 percent, and no general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so fundamentals carry the forecast. The combination of a deep-blue electorate, a well-funded incumbent, and a financially dormant opponent makes an upset highly unlikely. The main open question is the size of the winning margin rather than the outcome, with the district's underlying lean favoring the Democrat by roughly 27 points.
